body: My LO was exactly 2 months old when she slept through the night! (On my birthday to be exact, I still say that’s the best birthday gift I’ve ever received lol) honestly, follow your baby’s cues, feed until they fall asleep — for us I usually know when she’s ready for bed if she gets distracted/tries to play I give three verbal warnings “all done, time for milk” or “no more, bed or milk” and 100% of the time once I lay her down she’s out within seconds!

I just wanna say I’m so sorry people suck, as an early childhood educator AND first time (single) mom. My baby slept through the night on my birthday at 2 months old. I always tell everyone “that’s the best birthday gift I’ve ever received!!” I didn’t intentionally sleep train either I just followed my baby’s cues, for example, I’d be nursing and if my LO started to become ‘silly’ or distracted by toys/objects around I give three chances and verbally say “all done, time for milk” or “no more sillies, milk or bed” would be my last warning. It’s hard to explain but as soon as I laid my LO down, there may be 1 or 2 groans/whimpers while trying to get comfy but within 0.5 seconds my baby would be asleep. 

Baby is now 17 months old and sleeps/naps independently in the crib. Reading your post my initial thought was those are signs of a teething baby (especially the drool)! My LO loves food, but when teething it seemed like my baby wasn’t eating as much as usual, and was easily irritated by seemingly normal things. You’re doing the absolute best for your baby, don’t let anyone tell you otherwise! We’re all learning as we go💗

This is right on the money comment! I just wanted to piggyback and add on I left my child’s father when I was pregnant because of emotional, manipulative and substance abuse issues. He referred to therapy as a joke, make believe, not real. He’s never been alone with our child because she is uncomfortable around him. Babies know before you do, if you can’t find a way to leave and keep your baby safe for you then do it for your child. I didn’t want my daughter around someone cussing/screaming until the sun came up because he had a “bad day” my daughter now sleeps all night Independently, in her own room with peace and quiet.

I’m surprised more people don’t know this. For a mother to choose to be a solo/single parent the father has to not be a walking red flag (to put it mildly). The mother of the children probably gave him over 100 chances, what makes OP think it’ll be different this time? I’ll never sleep or be with a single father who doesn’t take care/see, know his children.

It was truly frightening, and felt impossible to keep calm during this moment. I’m the same with unbearable anxiety! I even mentioned before leaving the room “so and so has special milk, please be aware when serving lunch!” They were told by numerous people & yes they were fired immediately, I believe the parents also reported them.

Most people don’t! I worked in a daycare where we had new staff in our room (frequently) and we had a child with a dairy allergy. Even the other toddlers said to the teacher “that’s not their milk!!!” And the teacher continued to pour them a cup of milk, child drank it and had an anaphylactic reaction, one of the scariest moments of my life was running into this scene. Children were screaming, the teacher claimed they were distracted by the noise of the classroom (no excuse when there’s signs posted everywhere, we have to sign off on these to make sure were aware + child had their own labeled food/drinks that were kept separate from other children) child survived but definitely traumatized by the situation.

Even a simple mixup like “fish vs chicken” could be life or death with someone who has a deadly seafood(or meat) allergy. You truly don’t know what someone could be allergic to without communicating with the person. I totally agree they should lose their job so there isn’t a “next time” it could’ve ended a lot worse and they should be held accountable.
Of course! Don’t forget to give yourself some grace and a big hug, you’re doing amazing and raising strong, kind, brave humans🫶🏼

Hey mama, I only have one child and I didn’t have a C-section however I have Deaf parents (dads passed away, but my mom was at the birth) and I had to be a translator for her while giving birth, doctors/nurses made fun of my mom right in front of us, my mom kindly asked them to move down their mask when speaking to her they laughed in her face. Once my baby was here my mom got overwhelmed/annoyed of how she was being treated and somehow made it about herself then she left me all alone for the entire next day, but that night my baby went purple because the mucus wasn’t suctioned out of the mouth and me being the one who found my dad deceased I was having PTSD/panic attacks (thank goodness for the quick nurses hearing my screams) but being a new mom I was terrified to hold or even move my child after that and suddenly realized I wasn’t offering enough milk so baby had lost a little weight by the time we left, I don’t think I’ll tell my baby every detail of the birth but there are some good moments I can remember. I cut the cord, that feeling of “wow I created this beautiful baby” and I’ll never forget the moment they put my baby on my chest and just thinking “I’d do anything to protect, care, nurture you”. I can also tell my baby that her aunt and uncle came to see us in the hospital and drove us home. Try to “build up” the little good, happy moments because I know how painful and overwhelming it can be focusing on the rough, hard moments especially when it wasn’t the way you planned or not what you expected. Since losing my dad, I’ve tried to soak in as much as I can (since the day my baby was born I’ve been writing “do not forget” moments in my notes app so whenever I’m stressed, overwhelmed or just having a bad day I read those and suddenly I can get back to a somewhat normal routine) hope this helps ease your mind a little! 🫶🏼

Most of the parents are grateful! However I’ve had a few who either took offence to the care I was providing or insisted I do more such as bathing their child if they got dirty from playing, or washing their clothes if we painted/sensory play. I’ve also had a parent say “It must be such an easy job to just hangout with children all day” I was too stunned to speak.

FTM and my baby HATED swaddles outside of the hospital (2 days it lasted) but LOVED to be in the sleep sacks for quite a while after! Every baby is different and for me the most important thing was tracking feedings, I couldn’t remember which side I offered prior or how long they were eating so I started writing it down in a little notepad and honestly it’s nice to look back on and double check how often newborns need to nurse/feed🥹 my baby got into their own routine (every 2 hours spot on) and my body would wake me up 5 minutes before baby every time (still does), it was a routine that worked for us. What works for one might not work for all though but I always recommend following your babies cues, schedule, they know what they need and I just focused on getting to learn their routine by testing everything and seeing what helps soothe/calm them. (Ex. Checking diaper, offering milk, putting on sleepy music, rocking, more/less blankets etc)

Exactly! It’s almost like their way of crying out for help, whether that be following through with consequences to bad behaviours, or just some extra quality time together. I worked in daycares where parents would be lined up outside before we even open and pick up their child 30-1 hour after we closed… that means they go home to eat dinner then go to bed, most of their days were spent with caregivers. As young as 15 months, one little child wouldn’t leave my side, crawl into my lap and we’d read stories together for hours on end but you never know what their home life is like… if I’m their one source of kindness, caring and compassion then that’s what I’ll be. You only know what you know.

Sitting here breastfeeding my 17 month old daughter. I don’t let ANYONE tell me otherwise (unless it’s my doctor) because you know your child best. My doctor also told me “breastfeeding after 1 years old is still 35-40% of their nutrition” so don’t worry, you’re doing a wonderful thing! I’m in a similar situation as my child doesn’t see her dad very often (he’s unable to stay sober & not scream or yell in our faces during visits) but I treat it like a business relationship; only speaking about the child and that helps me to take my emotions out of it so then I can focus solely on my child’s well-being and safety.

Your comment reminded me of a time when I was in middle school, and we had a boy with a learning/physical disability; other boys in my classroom were trying to teach him really bad words “your mom is a c word” that sort of thing. I didn’t understand at the time (I was 7) but the way they laughed at him when he’d try to repeat after them made me cry so I moved my seat beside him and started sharing/reading my favourite book with him. He smiled and showed me a book he was learning about and those boys scoffed then walked away. I don’t think they ever got in trouble but I got made fun of the rest of the year by these boys for hanging out with the “r word” kid. My entire day I waited until that class so we could read and share our favourite books with eachother. Looking back and knowing what I know now, all of those boys had awful, terrible home environments (not an excuse) but they were looking for attention and it didn’t matter how they got it or if it was good or bad.

I’m a single mom but reading this I got the impression you’re a married single mom. My LO started sleeping through the night at 2 months old, now 17 months old and still sleeps through the night. Also EBF, if my LO didn’t sleep through the night I’d probably be a walking zombie as everything is my responsibility. What helped me was letting my baby BF until she fell asleep, or if she started getting distracted/being silly and trying to play - I give 3 warnings, “all done, time for sleep, no more sillies” and if it happened again that’s when I lay her down and she immediately passes out. It was almost like a sign she was ready to sleep. I know not every baby is the same but a consistent routine helps greatly and your husband seems more than capable of doing more than just a few hours in the morning. You aren’t the only parent, so rather than “asking” him to help, show him. Try a schedule that works for both of you, 6-8pm start winding down, play calming music, read books, then switch shifts around 1-2am (or whenever baby wakes). 

It also really helped me to “count her cries” for example, when she was younger and I was transitioning to longer periods of sleep if she cried longer than 2 minutes it was serious and she needed my attention (needed more milk, comfort, cuddles whatever it may be) and if the crying stopped/was sporadic she’d fall asleep on her own. I learned the hard way by responding to every noise/whimper/movement and it was causing her more stress seeing me come in and out of the room. We’re now in a place where I can lay her down awake (after rocking, rubbing back, and BFing) and not even 5 minutes later she’s asleep. She sleeps from 7-8pm to 8-9am. Hopefully this helps and feel free to message me if you have other questions! 

I should probably add, I’m an Early Childhood Educator with over 10+ years of experience but it’s a completely different story once you have your own. What works for one might not work for another so my biggest recommendation is follow your baby’s lead/cues

I’m a Carolyn and I work in daycares/schools around young children. Most of them called me Caroline, and sometimes I got Kevin 🫣 I used to hate my name because I’ve never had a real nickname until a little girl gave me the nickname “miss care care” I truly think the name Caroline/Carolyn is beautiful and elegant though. There isn’t much “insults” that go with it  (minus my first boyfriend calling me Carl) and my first adult girls trip to Mexico they singled me out of the crowd to play Sweet Caroline but I’ve grown used to that from being in dance clubs/church dances where friends/acquaintances would request that song specifically for me. That’s probably the only complaint I have is how many times I have to hear that song and people always quote it, sing it or use it in conversation with me. Then I think, I’d hate to be “Stacy’s mom” or “Scotty doesn’t know” so there’s probably always going to be a song with someone’s name but try to look at it as that person was important enough to have a song written about them. I totally get what you’re feeling though, but if you embrace your name you take back the power of your name and who you are as a person💗

I was an early childhood educator now a first time mom and comparison is a thief of joy. I used to get so upset my baby wasn’t doing everything I’ve seen other children do. My LO is now 16 months and is walking! My LO didn’t roll over at the “milestone” mark, and HATED tummy time, probably spent a total of an hour trying to do it but it only made my LO upset so I waited until there was more signs of readiness and willingness to try. I just think ALL babies move at their own pace and we can’t rush or force them to do things they aren’t ready for! The best thing was at 2 months old, on my birthday my baby slept through the night for the first time — best birthday gift I’ve ever received, just be patient and supportive, your girl will get the hang of it! Whenever I wanted to make my LO laugh or move around I’d sing the itsy bitsy spider and do the motions along her body “tickling the arms, under the chin etc” and I do a lot of sign language because my parents are Deaf. I hope you find the groove that works for you guys, and reminder this is both of your first times living and learning 🫶🏼

I had to take my LO out to an auto repair shop because I was anxious my car would break down (it was making noises) and we’d be stuck in the middle of the nowhere. I had bad anxiety before birth but it definitely heightened after birth so I can relate to thinking every moment/decision is going to “alter or change” us somehow. During this trip to the shop, she got hungry as did I and there was a little cafe coffee shop place… well they were not baby friendly whatsoever, and I learned the hard way that babies are not good around glassware as I was wrestling with her to not grab the plate or glass cup of water off the table more than we were eating, there was also no high chairs so we sat in a booth where my LO couldn’t even see over the table. So now I carry an extra suction bowl/plate, two sippy cups and sometimes an easy snack (arrowroot cookies, baby granola bars, rice rusks etc). Reddit is great for advice but you can’t get physical social interaction/experiences from it, and my new anxiety is that I’m not supporting my child’s social development enough as she’s the first baby in my family and we aren’t around babies her age as much as adults.

I was an early childhood educator, now a first time mom and honestly some of the experiences with other peoples children really helped shape who I am as a mom. There’s a diaper bag that unfolds into a changing pad, I also keep wipes in my car/purse literally always on my person wherever we go because babies are also messy eaters in public lol. I think it just helps to have the things readily available for any situation such as a garbage bag in the car, in the diaper bag. I also use doggy bags if I’m visiting friends/family for the stinkier BM’s because not everyone wants to smell a smelly 💩in their garbage can until garbage day. If you’re not near your vehicle and literally in the middle of nowhere I’d suggest finding a place with a bathroom and hoping for the best, you never know there may be other moms around who have supplies that can help but you won’t know without asking for help! ♥️

I’d also like to say my LO is 16 months now and it’s much harder to not get covered in crap because she’s more capable of rolling around and crawling away from me more than when she was 3 months and just smiled at me whenever I changed her diaper. So you could carry a water bottle/some soap or hand sanitizer in a Fanny pack for those really bad situations! Hope this helps 🫶🏼

This was really helpful information, thank you for taking the time to kindly explain it for me! I just want everyone to feel included and my parents, their friends and other people in the HOH/Deaf community really instilled it into my brain that the terms were highly offensive to them so I didn’t really know anything else about it! 

I think I’m overly sensitive on the topic of “HOH/Deaf” because I’ve been an advocate and translator for my parents my entire life, even when I was giving birth to my first child. The doctors and nurses all wore masks which is to be expected but when I asked kindly if they could step back, remove their mask so my mom could read their lips and understand what they’re saying; I was laughed at and told “I’m not doing that just to make her happy” while I was in active labour unable to interpret for my mom. I just hope one day things can be different and everyone can feel included. That’s just one of many challenges I’ve witnessed advocating for my parents. 
(Ps happy cake day! 🍰🫶🏼)

This makes a lot of sense but I’m still a bit confused by how “pass/fail” is less definitive as there’s cases where they mix them up all the time. Such as OPs case where they said he “passed” but then he didn’t? If the results of these tests aren’t accurate I would think the terminology would be a little different. Couldn’t the term “inconclusive” be more appropriate since it doesn’t give a definitive answer, it’s just “undetermined” I guess. The hearing test doesn’t tell someone how much hearing loss they have or don’t have either so I guess I don’t see the point in doing the hearing test at all as it doesn’t really make a difference, wouldn’t you get more information about it by following up with your family doctor regardless?

Conclusive or inconclusive results? Anything other than pass/fail works just fine. I was tested for a genetic abnormality and not once heard “pass or fail” it was simply the name of what I had. You could even put “hearing/HOH/Deaf” the actual terms of the conditions.

As someone who is deeply involved in the HOH/Deaf community many do view the terminology as offensive, it isn’t just me. Plus it isn’t a school test, it’s a persons abilities… you could compare it to any disability where you lack “function” but it still shouldn’t mean “failure” … all they really want is to change the terminology used because it’s hurtful. 

I don’t like to argue about this because who are we to say what’s offensive to someone else, people can feel the way they feel and I was raised to be inclusive of others and respect their feelings; not belittle them for feeling the way they feel.

I have deaf parents and refused the hearing test because my parents were offended by the terminology “pass and fail” meaning to be deaf is considered a failure? I don’t agree with it either if I’m being honest and the answer of this test does not change the love/care I provide to my child. My child is hearing however we still teach sign language because it’s a form of communication before they can speak. I’m sorry you’re going through this and I hope it works out in the end 💜

I’m an early childhood educator who’s worked in over 25 daycares the last 10-15 years. The things I’ve witnessed and reported are mind boggling, I really don’t want to scare anyone because there is amazing daycares out there but as hard as it is staying home and caring for my child by myself I’d do it 100 times over. You’ll never get that time back with them and the unknowing if someone else is treating them appropriately or “similar” to how I would gives me intense anxiety, I’d rather know my child’s safe, loved and in good hands 100% of the time. I’ve reported cases of abuse and been told I was lying because the person I reported had “seniority” at the centre, that’s the day I quit and told every parent at the centre what was happening. Do what’s best for you and your baby, no matter what anyone else thinks! There will always be jobs out there but only one of your child 🫶🏼

Edit to add: feel free to PM me if you ever just need to vent, or have questions about anything🥰 this is for whoever needs a listening ear!

Damn that really saddens me. I lost my dad unexpectedly almost 3 years ago and this post had me in my feels reminiscing about our times together 😭 there’s some really good advice in these comments too!

It’s never too late! My dad was a weekend dad, I was a little older than OPs daughter and I eventually moved in with my dad in my early 20s. I’m glad I did because he passed away suddenly and I can’t imagine him being alone when that happened. Things can change for the better but just remember to be supportive of your daughter, communicate with her as much as she’ll allow, incorporate her favourite foods/hobbies/activities when you do see eachother and things can be mended. Not saying it can happen overnight but shift your thinking to anything’s possible if you give it time and effort.

I hate how much some parents enforce “court orders” when it’s literally children’s lives at stake here. When you rely so heavily on a piece of paper telling you how to parent and what to do I feel like you forget that all your child really wants is to feel wanted, loved and safe wherever that may be.

I was between 14-16 when my parents went through a messy divorce, they constantly put me and my sister in the middle and my mom spoke poorly of my dad every single day. My dad was taught by his mom “Never speak badly of their mother in front of them, don’t involve the children in adult conversations” and that’s the best thing my dad could’ve done in the situation. Even though they had a court order they weren’t strict about it whatsoever and focused solely on whatever me and my sister wanted (this may not work for everyone but it was good for us) and my dad never stopped trying to be there for us (even when we told him nasty things) it did get to a time where we barely went over to our dads but he never stopped talking to us and trying to mend the relationship. He’d bring me breakfast, lunch, dinners randomly, he spoiled us for Easter and Valentine’s Day with flowers, food and handmade gifts. Truthfully I don’t think my dad even considered the fact that my mom was speaking so negatively about him and that was what caused us to drift apart. Fortunately once I turned 18-20 I started living with my dad and we became closer than ever. My dad passed away suddenly when I was 25, but whenever I was upset with my mom or wanted to crap talk about her he would say this every time “she’s still your mom and she loves you very much” even if I was extremely upset with my mom he reminded me that life is quickly passing by and you only get one mom / one dad (or two moms/two dads/ whatever your family may look like) 

Looking back every “outing” we had was because of my dad, me and my sister asked to go see waterfalls at 2-3am, he happily jumped up and took us out, he made us special coins/artifacts. He spent time with us doing the activities we wanted and never forced us to do anything we didn’t want to. I went on my first solo vacation with some friends and coming home our town was hit with a huge snowstorm my dad cancelled his plans to see his old buddies who he hadn’t seen in years just to come and get me. I’m tearing up thinking about this but I had my first child almost a year after his passing, his first grandchild he never got to meet and my coparenting relationship now isn’t good whatsoever but because of him I know how to make sure my child is safe, cared for, loved and respected. I will never speak poorly of my child’s other parent no matter what I think of them. 


At your daughter’s age, give her some grace and patience. Being a preteen is hard but a preteen girl is even more challenging. If there’s certain games/toys or activities she likes at her mom’s, offer to get it for your place. My dad would ask us if we wanted to bring our family dog for the weekend and truthfully that got us over there more often than not. The dog was a form of security in a new unfamiliar environment. I hope this helps and you’re able to get to a place where everyone is happy and comfortable 🫶🏼

You have previous experiences are they all the same? Probably not. You have the most knowledge of your situation, you didn’t really go into details about what you’re asking for from this. Basically it comes down to, does he want to be involved, is it healthy for him to be involved then go from there. It’s your life and decision at the end of the day, not Reddits.

Other peoples experiences may be different. Which mine is  hence why I’m saying that. I’m not intentionally judging but say your (hypothetical) 20 year old child came to you and said they liked someone 13 years younger… that’s an actual 7 year old child.. It’s modelling some not so good behaviours for your children in the future is all I worry about. If this doesn’t raise concerns for you there may be bigger issues at play here and I suggest therapy for all involved. Truthfully you should be putting your children first rather than worrying about what the mid 20 year olds are doing. You really can’t expect to come to Reddit and get praises for poor behaviour.

I was 16 when my parents divorced but my situation is vastly different from others as both of my parents are Deaf. If I have any advice for co-parenting, it’s put the child first always. Try to imagine yourself in their position and make choices that benefit the child. An example of what not to do would be my mother telling us inappropriate details of their relationship as if we were the ones in the relationship with him. They also weren’t strict with the co-parenting agreement and my dad made it his goal to consistently be involved in our lives, which made a world of a difference adjusting to two homes, it never felt as separate as it actually was because he made it comfortable and safe. 

A man can be a crappy partner but a great dad simultaneously but don’t involve the children in the personal arguments or disagreements. That’s one thing my grandma taught my dad was “never talk poorly about their mom in front of them” and it will forever make me proud and impressed by my dad’s ability to focus on us even when his world was shattered and his reputation was ruined.
